definition: Allegory means a story in which the characters and events stand for deeper moral or political meanings.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word allegory. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know allegory should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: On its surface the ballet is a nursery quarrel between wind-up toys; critics read it as an allegory of the museum's own funding wars.
A symbol is a single charged image — one dove, one broken clock — while an allegory keeps a whole cast of symbols working together from the first page to the last.
A parable stops short of allegory: it builds one small story to make one point, while an allegory threads its second meaning through every scene of a larger work.

A symbolic tale is a story that leans on symbols here and there — an image or two carrying extra weight. An allegory goes much further: it keeps a sustained one-to-one mapping, so nearly every character and event has a counterpart from the first scene to the last.

A coded story hides a second, intended meaning under its surface, often so that only insiders will find it. An allegory also carries a second meaning, but openly and completely: any attentive reader can unfold the mapping, and it runs through the whole work rather than staying buried.
